title: bank of england / quantitative easing / qe | Monetary Policy Report | Quantitative easing
summary: The Bank of England provides an explanatory overview of its quantitative easing (QE) programme, a monetary policy tool used to lower long-term borrowing costs when Bank Rate is near zero. The UK QE programme purchased a total of £895 billion in bonds (£875bn government gilts, £20bn corporate bonds), with the last expansion announced in November 2020. The Bank is currently in quantitative tightening (QT) mode, having begun bond runoff in February 2022 as inflation is above the 2% target.
